notes.text: Session logic is in src/auth/session.ts: sessions are server-side in Redis (key prefix `sess:`) with a 14-day sliding expiry, and the browser only gets the opaque `tandem_sid` cookie (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax).
notes.question_query: where do we store user sessions?
notes.update: Moved login sessions from Redis into a Postgres `auth_sessions` table; Redis was evicting keys under memory pressure and logging people out at random.
notes.related: Admin impersonation gets its own session with `impersonatorId` set, and it's hard-capped at 1 hour no matter how active it is.

notes.text: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, cost 12. Don't lower the cost to speed up tests; the test env already sets BCRYPT_ROUNDS=4.
notes.question_query: what algorithm are user passwords hashed with?
notes.update: Switched password hashing to argon2id. Existing bcrypt hashes still verify and get re-hashed with argon2 on the user's next successful login.
notes.related: Signup and password change reject passwords shorter than 10 characters, plus anything found in the HIBP breached-password range API.

notes.text: Public API auth = per-workspace API keys with `tdm_live_` / `tdm_test_` prefixes. Only a SHA-256 hash is stored, so the plaintext key is shown once at creation and can't be recovered.
notes.question_query: how do third-party integrations authenticate against our API?
notes.update: The public API uses OAuth2 client credentials now: integrations exchange a client ID and secret for a bearer token that lasts an hour. Static API keys have been retired.
notes.related: API keys can be scoped read-only; write endpoints check with the `requireScope('write')` middleware and return 403 for read-only keys.

notes.text: Prod migrations are run by hand (`pnpm db:migrate` from the bastion host); the deploy pipeline never touches the schema.
notes.question_query: how do schema migrations get applied in production?
notes.update: Migrations run automatically now as a `migrate` job in the deploy workflow, before the new containers go live. Don't run them by hand against prod anymore.
notes.related: Schema changes have to work with both the old and the new code (expand/contract): add the column as nullable, backfill it, and drop the old one in a later PR.

notes.text: Gotcha: DATABASE_URL goes through PgBouncer in transaction mode, so prepared statements, advisory locks, LISTEN/NOTIFY and session-level SET won't work on it. Use DATABASE_DIRECT_URL for anything that needs a real session.
notes.question_query: why do prepared statements fail against the database?
notes.update: PgBouncer is gone and DATABASE_URL connects straight to Postgres again, so advisory locks, LISTEN/NOTIFY and prepared statements work on the main pool. DATABASE_DIRECT_URL was removed.
notes.related: Each API container's pg pool is capped at 10 connections (PG_POOL_MAX) and the worker uses 4; check PgBouncer's default_pool_size before raising either.

notes.text: Projects and tasks are soft-deleted via a `deleted_at` column, and a nightly purge job hard-deletes anything that's been in the trash for more than 30 days.
notes.question_query: what happens to a project row when a user deletes it?
notes.update: Deleting a project or task now removes the row immediately. If something needs restoring, use the JSON snapshot written to audit_log at delete time; there's no trash period anymore.
notes.related: Queries on tasks and projects have to skip trashed rows; the `notDeleted()` query helper adds the `deleted_at IS NULL` filter for you.

notes.text: Deploy flow: merging to main auto-deploys to staging, but prod only ships when someone runs the 'Promote to production' workflow in GitHub Actions, which needs a maintainer's approval.
notes.question_query: how does a merged change get released to production?
notes.update: Prod deploys are continuous now: a merge to main goes to staging and then straight on to production once the smoke tests pass. No manual promote step.
notes.related: .github/workflows/deploy.yml builds the Docker image once per commit and promotes that same tag to prod, so prod runs exactly what was tested on staging.

notes.text: Prod is AWS ECS Fargate in us-east-1 (api + worker services; the React app is static on S3/CloudFront), all managed by Terraform in infra/terraform/. Don't change anything by hand in the console.
notes.question_query: what cloud infrastructure does production run on?
notes.update: Production moved to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) for EU data residency; us-east-1 only hosts staging now.
notes.related: Terraform state is in the `tandem-tf-state` S3 bucket with DynamoDB locking. Run `make plan ENV=prod` and paste the output into the PR before anyone applies.

notes.text: Secrets live in SSM Parameter Store under /tandem/<env>/ and get injected into the ECS tasks as env vars at deploy time. Nothing secret goes in the repo, not even staging values.
notes.question_query: where should I put a new API secret for production?
notes.update: Secrets are managed in Doppler now. The containers pull them at startup with a Doppler service token, and the old SSM parameters are being deleted.
notes.related: A new env var also has to be added to the zod schema in src/config/env.ts; the app refuses to boot if a required one is missing.

notes.text: Integration tests need the Postgres from docker-compose.test.yml (port 5433, start it with `pnpm test:db:up`); each test runs in a transaction that gets rolled back afterwards.
notes.question_query: how do I set up a database for running the integration tests locally?
notes.update: Integration tests spin up their own Postgres through Testcontainers (one per Vitest worker), so there's nothing to start beforehand; just run the tests.
notes.related: Integration specs are the *.int.test.ts files. Plain `pnpm test` skips them, so use `pnpm test:int` to run those.

notes.text: Playwright E2E only runs on PRs with the `run-e2e` label, plus nightly on main. It takes ~15 min, so it's deliberately not part of the default PR checks.
notes.question_query: why didn't the Playwright tests run on my PR?
notes.update: E2E runs on every PR now, sharded across 4 runners (about 5 minutes total). No label needed.
notes.related: E2E specs log in with the `loginAs(page, 'owner')` fixture, which creates the session directly instead of going through the login form.

notes.text: CI fails the `test` job if line coverage for src/ drops below 80% (the threshold is set in vitest.config.ts).
notes.question_query: does CI enforce a minimum coverage percentage?
notes.update: Coverage is report-only in CI now: the PR comment still shows the numbers, but a drop doesn't fail the build anymore.
notes.related: Generated code (src/generated/) and test helpers are excluded from the coverage numbers via `coverage.exclude`.

notes.text: Styling convention: Tailwind only, no CSS modules or styled-components. Take colors and spacing from the theme in tailwind.config.ts instead of hardcoding hex values.
notes.question_query: how should I style a new component?
notes.update: We're migrating off Tailwind. New components get a co-located .module.css that uses the CSS variables in web/src/styles/tokens.css, and Tailwind classes get converted whenever a file is touched.
notes.related: Dark mode uses Tailwind's `class` strategy (ThemeProvider toggles `dark` on <html>), so use `dark:` variants rather than prefers-color-scheme media queries.

notes.text: UI primitives are Radix, wrapped in our own components in web/src/components/ui/ (Button, Dialog, Select, Tooltip, ...). Feature code should import from there, never from @radix-ui/* directly.
notes.question_query: where should feature code import dialogs and dropdowns from?
notes.update: It's fine to import @radix-ui/react-* directly in feature code now. We're deleting the pass-through wrappers in components/ui and only keeping the ones that add real styling or behavior (Button, Dialog).
notes.related: Each component in components/ui has a Storybook story next to it; `pnpm storybook` serves them on :6006 if you want to check the variants.

notes.text: Icons: lucide-react only, don't add another icon library. Size 16 in tables and menus, 20 everywhere else.
notes.question_query: which icon library are we using?
notes.update: Icons are Phosphor (@phosphor-icons/react) now as part of the rebrand. lucide-react is being removed, so please don't add new lucide imports.
notes.related: Icons that lucide doesn't have (our logo mark, the Slack and Stripe integration logos) are hand-written SVG components in web/src/icons/.

notes.text: API errors always come back as `{ error: { code, message } }` with a stable snake_case `code` (e.g. `task_not_found`). Clients should branch on `code`, never on the message text.
notes.question_query: what JSON shape should an API error return?
notes.update: Error responses follow RFC 7807 now: application/problem+json with type, title, status and detail, and the machine-readable code is the last segment of the `type` URI.
notes.related: Validation failures are 422 and also include `error.details`, which maps field paths to messages, e.g. `{ "dueDate": ["must be in the future"] }`.

notes.text: List endpoints use cursor pagination: `?limit=` (max 100) plus `?cursor=`, and responses include `nextCursor` (null on the last page). No offset or page-number params anywhere.
notes.question_query: how do list endpoints handle paging?
notes.update: List endpoints switched to `page`/`pageSize` with a `total` in the response, since the reports table needs page numbers. The cursor params are gone.
notes.related: Cursors are opaque base64 of (created_at, id). Clients shouldn't decode them, and a cursor is only valid for the sort order it was issued with.

notes.text: Public API versioning is in the path (/v1/...). Additive changes like new optional fields or new endpoints can go into v1; anything breaking needs a new version.
notes.question_query: how do we ship a breaking change to the public API?
notes.update: API versions are now picked with a dated `Tandem-Version` header (Stripe-style, e.g. 2026-09-01) instead of a URL prefix, and new routes are mounted without /v1.
notes.related: Before removing a field we send `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on responses that include it, at least 90 days ahead.

notes.text: Stripe webhooks are processed synchronously in src/billing/webhooks.ts: the subscription row is updated within the request and we only return 200 after the commit, so Stripe retries if anything throws.
notes.question_query: how are incoming Stripe events processed?
notes.update: The Stripe webhook endpoint now just verifies the signature, saves the raw event to `stripe_events` and returns 200 right away; a background job applies the subscription changes.
notes.related: Signature verification needs the raw body, so /webhooks/stripe is mounted with express.raw() before the global express.json() in src/server.ts. Don't reorder that middleware.

notes.text: Stripe price IDs for each plan are mapped in src/billing/plans.ts, separately for test and live mode. Never hardcode a `price_...` ID anywhere else.
notes.question_query: where do the Stripe prices for each plan come from?
notes.update: Plans resolve their Stripe price by lookup_key (`team_monthly`, `team_annual`, etc.) at boot and cache it, so there are no price IDs in the code anymore.
notes.related: Annual plans are 10x the monthly price (two months free). When adding a plan, add both the monthly and the annual price, for test and live.

notes.text: Trials are 14 days with no credit card required. If a trial ends with no payment method on file, the workspace becomes read-only; nothing gets deleted.
notes.question_query: what happens to a workspace when its free trial ends?
notes.update: Signup requires a card now and trials are 7 days; at the end they convert to a paid subscription automatically unless the customer cancels.
notes.related: Trial workspaces get a reminder email 3 days before the end, triggered by Stripe's `customer.subscription.trial_will_end` event.

notes.text: Background jobs are on BullMQ. Each job type has its own handler file, and the worker runs as a separate process (`pnpm worker`), not inside the API server.
notes.question_query: which queue library do we use for async work?
notes.update: Swapped BullMQ for pg-boss, so jobs are rows in Postgres and can be enqueued in the same transaction as the write that triggers them.
notes.related: Jobs are split across separate queues (`email`, `billing`, `exports`) with their own concurrency, so a burst of CSV exports can't hold up outgoing email.

notes.text: Default job retry policy: 5 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 30s. Don't override it per job unless there's a specific reason.
notes.question_query: how many times is a failing job retried?
notes.update: Bumped the default to 10 attempts with backoff capped at 1h; during last week's email provider outage, jobs ran out of retries before it recovered.
notes.related: Since a retry can run after a partial success, handlers must be idempotent; e.g. send-invoice-email checks `invoices.emailed_at` before sending.

notes.text: Recurring jobs (usage rollup nightly at 02:00 UTC, trial-expiry sweep hourly) are registered in src/jobs/schedule.ts and run inside the worker; we don't use OS cron or scheduled GitHub Actions for this.
notes.question_query: where do I register a job that should run every night?
notes.update: Scheduled jobs fire from EventBridge Scheduler rules now (infra/terraform/schedules.tf), so they don't get skipped during worker deploys. src/jobs/schedule.ts was deleted.
notes.related: The usage rollup upserts on (workspace_id, day), so re-running it for a given date is safe: `pnpm job:run usage-rollup --date=2026-09-30`.

notes.text: Log through the pino instance from src/lib/logger.ts, and use `req.log` inside route handlers so the request ID gets attached. No console.log in server code.
notes.question_query: what's the right way to log from a route handler?
notes.update: Logging goes through the OpenTelemetry logs SDK now, so every line carries trace and span IDs. Import `log` from src/observability/log.ts; the pino logger module was removed.
notes.related: Never log request bodies on auth or billing routes. The logger redacts password/token/authorization fields, but redaction won't catch new field names.

notes.text: Sentry samples 10% of transactions for performance tracing in prod and 100% on staging; errors are always captured regardless of that rate.
notes.question_query: what sample rate do we use for performance traces in production?
notes.update: Dropped prod tracesSampleRate to 0.02 because we kept hitting the Sentry transaction quota mid-month. Staging still traces everything.
notes.related: The deploy workflow creates a Sentry release named after the git SHA and uploads the web app's source maps, so minified stack traces resolve.

notes.text: Our only alerting is Better Stack pinging /healthz every 30s and posting to #tandem-alerts in Slack. There's no PagerDuty, so nobody gets phoned.
notes.question_query: how do we find out when production goes down?
notes.update: Critical prod alerts now page the on-call engineer through PagerDuty; #tandem-alerts only gets the non-urgent stuff.
notes.related: /healthz only says the process is up; /readyz also checks the database connection and is what the load balancer health check hits.

notes.text: All UI strings go through i18next (`t('billing.upgradeCta')`) with files at web/src/locales/<lang>/<namespace>.json. English is the source language, and we only ship en and de right now.
notes.question_query: which languages does the app ship in?
notes.update: French and Spanish went live this week, so we're at four languages. Crowdin syncs the translations and opens PRs into the locales folder.
notes.related: Don't reuse a translation key across features just because the English text matches; German often needs different wording depending on context.

notes.text: Dates are stored in UTC and rendered in the user's profile timezone (users.timezone), not the browser's; format them with the helpers in web/src/lib/dates.ts.
notes.question_query: which timezone should timestamps be displayed in?
notes.update: Times are shown in the browser's local timezone now; we removed the timezone field from profile settings because it confused people who travel.
notes.related: `formatDate()` takes 'short' or 'long' and follows the UI language, so German users get 12.10.2026 instead of 10/12/2026.

notes.text: The dashboard stats endpoint (GET /workspaces/:id/stats) is cached in Redis for 60s per workspace. Call `invalidateStats(workspaceId)` after any write that changes task counts.
notes.question_query: how do we keep the dashboard stats endpoint fast?
notes.update: Workspace stats come from the `workspace_stats` materialized view, refreshed every 5 minutes. The Redis cache and invalidateStats() were removed, so counts can lag a bit.
notes.related: The stats endpoint was ~900ms p95 for large workspaces before caching; the composite index on tasks(workspace_id, status) also roughly halved the uncached query.

notes.text: Every top-level route is lazy-loaded with React.lazy, and the main bundle has a 250 KB gzipped budget that size-limit enforces in CI.
notes.question_query: how big is the main JS bundle allowed to be?
notes.update: Main bundle budget raised to 350 KB gzipped. The rich-text editor pushed us over and the user approved the increase.
notes.related: If the size check fails, `pnpm analyze` opens the rollup visualizer; it's usually a heavy lib (charts, editor) imported outside its lazy route.

notes.text: Lint/format is Biome, not ESLint or Prettier. `pnpm lint` runs `biome check` and CI fails on any diagnostic.
notes.question_query: are we using ESLint and Prettier?
notes.update: Back on ESLint + Prettier: we needed typescript-eslint's type-aware rules (no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises), and Biome doesn't have them.
notes.related: Formatter settings are 2-space indent, single quotes and trailing commas. `pnpm lint --write` fixes formatting, so don't hand-format around it.

notes.text: Pinned to Node 20 (.nvmrc, `engines`, node:20-alpine base image) because sharp's prebuilt binaries break on Node 22 with our Alpine image.
notes.question_query: can we upgrade to Node 22?
notes.update: Upgraded to Node 22 across the board; moving the Docker base image to node:22-bookworm-slim fixed the sharp install issue.
notes.related: CI's setup-node reads the version from .nvmrc (node-version-file), so there's no Node version hardcoded in the workflow files.

notes.text: Convention: named exports for components, hooks and utils, no `export default`. It keeps renames and find-all-references reliable.
notes.question_query: should components use default or named exports?
notes.update: Page components in web/src/pages/ are default exports now, so React.lazy(() => import('./pages/Billing')) works without the .then() remapping.
notes.related: The only files that should use `export default` are ones tools load by convention: the *.config.ts files and Storybook stories.

notes.text: Services signal failures by throwing the AppError subclasses from src/lib/errors.ts (NotFoundError, ForbiddenError, ConflictError), and the Express error middleware turns them into HTTP responses. Don't call res.status() from service code.
notes.question_query: how should a service report that a record wasn't found?
notes.update: Services return a Result (neverthrow ok/err) for expected failures instead of throwing, and route handlers map the error variant to a status code. Only throw for actual bugs.
notes.related: Each AppError takes the API error code as its first argument, e.g. `throw new NotFoundError('task_not_found')`, and that code ends up in the response body.

notes.text: User prefers small, single-purpose PRs (roughly under 400 changed lines), with refactors split out from behavior changes.
notes.question_query: how big should pull requests be for this user?
notes.update: User said they'd rather review one PR per feature, even a big one, than a stack of small dependent PRs, so stop splitting work up.
notes.related: For any UI change, the user wants before/after screenshots in the PR description.

notes.text: Check with the user before adding any new npm dependency: propose it with size and maintenance info instead of just running `pnpm add`.
notes.question_query: do I need to ask before installing a new package?
notes.update: User is OK with us adding dev dependencies (test utils, @types packages, build tooling) without asking; only runtime deps still need sign-off.
notes.related: When proposing a package, the user wants to see weekly downloads, last release date, gzipped size, and at least one alternative we considered.

notes.text: Before reporting a task as done, the user wants `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and the relevant tests run locally. Don't hand off and let CI find the problems.
notes.question_query: what should I run before telling the user a task is complete?
notes.update: User says there's no need to run the full typecheck and lint locally anymore since CI is fast now. Just run the tests for what you changed.
notes.related: If a check fails for something unrelated to the change (a flaky test, a type error already on main), the user wants it called out rather than quietly fixed in the same PR.

notes.text: Progress on CSV export: POST /exports and the `export-csv` job are merged; the Export button on the Reports page isn't started yet.
notes.question_query: how far along is the CSV export feature?
notes.update: CSV export is done end to end: the Reports page has a working Export button, and the download starts as soon as the job finishes.
notes.related: CSV exports are capped at 50k rows for now; anything bigger is out of scope until we add S3 delivery with an emailed download link.

notes.text: React 19 upgrade is on branch `chore/react-19`: typecheck passes but 6 Playwright specs fail around Dialog focus trapping, so it's not merged.
notes.question_query: has the React 19 upgrade landed yet?
notes.update: React 19 is merged to main. The Dialog focus failures went away after bumping the Radix packages.
notes.related: The React 19 branch also drops forwardRef from the components/ui wrappers, since ref is a regular prop now.
